Check what a streamed call needs, then simulate the call as
`voice streams simulate` does. It places no call and changes nothing.

Inbound, readiness <number>: the number is on this account with voice
enabled; an Indian (+91) number has an accepted compliance application; it
is routed to an application with an answer URL, which is then simulated with
the application's method. A missing fallback answer URL or hangup URL, and a
development tunnel, are warnings; a host Plivo cannot reach (this machine, a
private address) fails.

Outbound, readiness --from <caller ID> --to <number> --answer-url <url>: the
caller ID is a number on this account with voice enabled, or a verified
caller ID; an Indian caller ID has an accepted compliance application and
calls only Indian numbers; the account has cash credits. Geo permissions and
the concurrent call limit have no API, so they are unknown, never a pass.
--answer-method defaults to GET, as in `voice calls make`.

Each account check names the request it read. A number with no country
check says so. result is ready, not_ready, or unknown when nothing failed
but something could not be checked; the exit is 0 unless a check fails.
--dry-run makes the account reads but sends nothing to the answer URL. -o
json prints checks[] and the simulation; when a check fails, only the error,
with both in error.context.

Usage:
  plivo voice streams readiness [number] [flags]

Examples:
  plivo voice streams readiness +14155551234
  plivo voice streams readiness +14155551234 --xml-only -o json
  plivo voice streams readiness --from +14155551234 --to +14155555678 --answer-url https://agent.example.com/answer

Flags:
      --answer-method string   outbound: GET|POST (default "GET")
      --answer-url string      outbound: the answer URL the call will use
      --duration int           seconds of synthetic audio to stream (max 30) (default 3)
      --expect-audio           fail unless playAudio comes back; the audio is a tone, so only an echo-style agent or one that speaks first answers
      --from string            outbound: the caller ID, e.g. +14155551234
  -h, --help                   help for readiness
      --insecure               skip TLS verification (self-signed dev certs only)
      --to string              outbound: the number to call
      --xml-only               stop after the answer URL and its XML: open no WebSocket

Global Flags:
      --dry-run            preview requests and local changes without sending or writing anything
      --log-level string   log level: debug|info|warn|error|none (default "warn")
      --no-color           disable colored output
  -o, --output string      output format: table|json|jsonl|yaml|csv (default: table for TTY, json otherwise)
      --profile string     named profile from ~/.plivo/config.toml
      --query string       JMESPath filter on the JSON output, e.g. 'data.objects[].call_uuid' (implies -o json)
  -q, --quiet              suppress non-data output
      --schema             describe the command (arguments, flags, output fields) instead of running it
      --show-secrets       show auth tokens and passwords in API responses instead of [REDACTED]
      --timeout duration   request timeout: seconds, or a duration such as 90s or 2m (default 30s)
  -y, --yes                skip confirmation prompts
